Taskflow is the primary user-facing class representing a task dependency graph. It owns a Graph of Node objects, provides methods to add/inspect tasks via its FlowBuilder base, and utilities to query, clear, dump (DOT), and iterate tasks. Provides submission APIs (run, run_n, run_until), cooperative execution (corun, corun_until), async and dependent-async task submission (with and without futures), observer management, and status queries. Lifetime: construct with N>0, destructor waits for all work and joins workers. Thread-safety: most submission methods are thread-safe; observer manipulation is not. Requires types defined elsewhere (Worker, Taskflow, Node, Topology, etc.).

It does not own the underlying Node; it stores a Node* and provides APIs to set work (static, runtime, subflow, condition, multi-condition, module), manage dependencies, semaphores, name, user data, and query metadata (type, successors, predecessors). Runtime represents a per-task execution context used inside a running taskflow task to interact with the scheduler. Lightweight shared-ownership handle to a dependent asynchronous task managed by an executor. Behaves similarly to std::shared_ptr semantics for lifetime: reference count is stored in Node::DependentAsync::use_count within the associated Node. Provides status queries (empty, is_done, use_count), hashing, and exception access (exception_ptr, has_exception_ptr). Underlying Node, Node::DependentAsync, recycle, ESTATE, and Executor are declared elsewhere (graph.hpp).

Concurrency control primitive that limits the number of tasks allowed to run concurrently. Holds a maximum value and a current count; tasks acquire by decrementing when available and otherwise are queued as waiters. Thread-safe through an internal mutex. Friends Executor and Node use private helpers to acquire or release and to reschedule waiting tasks. Construction: default creates a zero-capacity semaphore; explicit constructor sets initial/max capacity. value() returns current tokens; max_value() returns capacity; reset() clears waiters and restores current to max (optionally changes max). Releasing beyond max throws via TF_THROW. Ownership: referenced by Node via waiting list; owned by no parent type in this header.

Nonblocking, lock-free style notifier that lets threads wait on a user predicate without holding a mutex. Threads use a two-phase protocol: prepare_wait -> recheck predicate -> commit_wait or cancel_wait. Notifications can wake pre-waiters or committed waiters via an internal epoch/stack state machine. Provides notify_one, notify_n, and notify_all. Lifetime: construct with capacity N, ensure no waiters remain at destruction. Thread-safe for intended operations.

Threading primitive offering lightweight, mutex-free notification/wait semantics based on an internal epoch and waiter count. It allows threads to prepare/cancel/commit waits and other threads to notify one/all/n waiters. Construction requires the number of waiters; destruction asserts that no waiter remains registered. Copy/move are disabled. Uses 64-bit atomics and relies on sequentially consistent fences for visibility.

Per-waiter state used by AtomicNotifier. Stores the epoch observed when the wait was prepared; alignment aims to avoid false sharing. Instances are owned and managed internally by AtomicNotifier in its _waiters vector.

functions.description: Constructs an AtomicNotifier managing N waiter slots for inter-thread synchronization. Intended to coordinate threads waiting on an external predicate using a lightweight, atomic-based protocol similar in spirit to a condition variable.

functions.description: Destructs the notifier. Asserts in debug builds that no threads are currently registered as waiters.

Destroying the notifier while there are active waiters is a programming error and may trip the assertion.

functions.name: tf::AtomicNotifier::notify_one
functions.description: Wakes at least one waiting thread, if any, by advancing the internal epoch and notifying a single waiter. Cheap when no threads are waiting.
requirements: May be called from any thread.
Safe to call even if there are no waiters; it becomes a no-op.
Callers should set/commit the external predicate before notifying, following the documented usage pattern.

functions.name: tf::AtomicNotifier::notify_all
functions.description: Wakes all currently waiting threads by advancing the internal epoch and issuing a broadcast notification. Cheap when no threads are waiting.
requirements: May be called from any thread.
Safe to call even if there are no waiters; it becomes a no-op.
Callers should set/commit the external predicate before notifying, following the documented usage pattern.

functions.name: tf::AtomicNotifier::notify_n
functions.description: Wakes up to n waiting threads by repeatedly issuing single notifications. If n >= size(), it behaves like notify_all().
requirements: n must be a non-negative size; if n >= size(), this function is equivalent to notify_all().
May be called from any thread and is safe when there are no waiters.
Callers should set/commit the external predicate before notifying, following the documented usage pattern.

functions.name: tf::AtomicNotifier::prepare_wait
functions.description: Registers the calling thread as a potential waiter at index w and captures the current epoch. Used as the first step in the wait protocol before re-checking the predicate.
requirements: w must be a valid waiter index in [0, size()).
Each concurrently waiting thread must use a unique index w to avoid data races on the internal waiter slot.
Must be followed by either cancel_wait(w) if the predicate becomes true, or commit_wait(w) to actually block.
Should be called only after an initial predicate check fails, per the documented usage pattern.

functions.name: tf::AtomicNotifier::cancel_wait
functions.description: Cancels a previously prepared wait at index w, decrementing the waiter count. Used when the predicate became true after prepare_wait.
requirements: w must be the same valid index previously passed to prepare_wait for the current thread.
Must be called only after a matching prepare_wait(w) and before any commit_wait(w).
Should be used when the second predicate check succeeds, per the documented usage pattern.

functions.name: tf::AtomicNotifier::commit_wait
functions.description: Blocks the calling thread at index w until a notifier advances the epoch, then unregisters the waiter. Used when the predicate is still false after prepare_wait and re-check.
requirements: w must be a valid waiter index in [0, size()) and correspond to a prior prepare_wait(w) that has not been canceled.
Should be called only when the predicate remains false after the second check; it will wait until notified.
Each concurrently waiting thread must use a unique index to avoid data races.
The caller must ensure the notifier object remains alive until the wait completes.

functions.name: tf::AtomicNotifier::num_waiters

functions.name: tf::make_for_each_task
functions.signature:
template <typename B, typename E, typename C, typename P = DefaultPartitioner>
auto tf::make_for_each_task(B b, E e, C c, P part = P());
functions.description: Builds a task functor that, when run with a Runtime&, applies the callable c to each element in the iterator range [b, e). The returned functor internally partitions the range using the provided partitioner P (DefaultPartitioner by default) and executes in parallel over the Runtime's executor when beneficial; otherwise it runs sequentially. Intended to be used with FlowBuilder::emplace or similar to create a Task. Details about Runtime, Partitioner, and Task types are provided by the surrounding Taskflow library.
requirements: B and E must form a valid half-open range [b, e) where std::distance(b, e) is well-defined.

B must be incrementable/advanceable; the code repeatedly calls std::advance and dereferences *beg, so the iterator must at least meet forward-iterator semantics (single-pass input iterators are likely unsafe for parallel partitioning).
Dereferencing and incrementing through [b, e) must be valid; c(*it) must be a valid expression for all it in [b, e).
C must be a callable invocable as c(value) where value is the dereferenced iterator value_type.

P must be a partitioner type compatible with the code (providing: type(), chunk_size(), adjusted_chunk_size(...), loop(...), and a call wrapper operator() that returns an invocable). DefaultPartitioner from the library satisfies this.
The function object returned must be invoked with a valid tf::Runtime& that provides executor().num_workers() and supports rt.silent_async(task).
Thread-safety: c may be invoked concurrently from multiple threads; it must be safe for concurrent calls and for the elements processed.
If N <= part.chunk_size() or there is only one worker, execution is sequential within the caller thread.

functions.name: tf::make_for_each_index_task
functions.signature:
template <typename B, typename E, typename S, typename C, typename P = DefaultPartitioner>
auto tf::make_for_each_index_task(B b, E e, S s, C c, P part = P());
functions.description: Builds a task functor that iterates indices or index-like values from b to e with step s and applies c to each index value. The returned functor partitions the iteration space using P and executes in parallel via the Runtime's executor when beneficial; otherwise it runs sequentially. If the index range is invalid (per is_index_range_invalid), the task is a no-op.
requirements: B, E, and S must define a valid index progression; is_index_range_invalid(b, e, s) must evaluate to false for work to proceed.
distance(b, e, s) must be well-defined and non-negative; N = distance(...) is used to size the iteration space.

For sequential path, the loop does: for (size_t x=0; x<N; ++x, beg += inc) c(beg); so B must support addition-assignment by S (operator+=) and dereference is not used; c is called with the current index value (same type as B).

For parallel path, code computes idx = static_cast<B_t>(part_b) * inc + beg; so B must support addition with S, and S must support multiplication by size_t; resulting expression type must be compatible with C's parameter type.
C must be a callable invocable as c(idx) where idx is the computed index value of type compatible with B + k*S.

P must be a partitioner type compatible with the code (providing: type() or P::type(), chunk_size(), adjusted_chunk_size(...), loop(...), and a call wrapper operator() that returns an invocable). DefaultPartitioner satisfies this.
The returned functor must be invoked with a valid tf::Runtime& that provides executor().num_workers() and supports rt.silent_async(task).
Thread-safety: c may be invoked concurrently from multiple threads; it must be safe for concurrent calls.
If N <= part.chunk_size() or there is only one worker, execution is sequential within the caller thread.

functions.name: tf::make_for_each_by_index_task
functions.signature:
template <typename R, typename C, typename P = DefaultPartitioner>
auto tf::make_for_each_by_index_task(R range, C c, P part = P());
functions.description: Builds a task functor that applies c to subranges (by index) of the given range object. The range R is expected to represent a discrete domain with begin(), end(), step_size(), size(), and discrete_domain(part_b, part_e). The functor partitions [0, R.size()) using P and calls c on either the whole range (sequential small case) or on R.discrete_domain(part_b, part_e) for each partition, enabling parallel execution via the Runtime's executor.
requirements: R must be a range-like type that provides begin(), end(), step_size(), size(), and discrete_domain(size_t part_b, size_t part_e).
The index range must be valid: is_index_range_invalid(r.begin(), r.end(), r.step_size()) must evaluate to false; otherwise no work is performed.
size() must return the total count N of discrete steps; N is used for partitioning and must fit in size_t.
C must be callable either as c(r) in the sequential path and as c(r.discrete_domain(part_b, part_e)) in the parallel path; both argument types must be acceptable to C.

P must be a partitioner type compatible with the code (providing: type(), chunk_size(), adjusted_chunk_size(...), loop(...), and a call wrapper operator() that returns an invocable). DefaultPartitioner satisfies this.
The returned functor must be invoked with a valid tf::Runtime& that provides executor().num_workers() and supports rt.silent_async(task).
Thread-safety: c may be invoked concurrently from multiple threads (on non-overlapping subranges); it must be safe for concurrent calls.
If N <= part.chunk_size() or there is only one worker, execution is sequential within the caller thread.

functions.name: tf::FlowBuilder::for_each
functions.signature:
template <typename B, typename E, typename C, typename P>
tf::Task tf::FlowBuilder::for_each(B beg, E end, C c, P part);
functions.description: Creates and emplaces a Task into the flow that applies c to each element in [beg, end) using the partitioner part. Internally wraps make_for_each_task(beg, end, c, part). Returns the created Task.
requirements: B and E must form a valid half-open range [beg, end) suitable for std::distance/advance and dereference; iterator should at least be forward-iterator to be safe under partitioned access.
C must be invocable as c(*it) for it in [beg, end).
P must be compatible with make_for_each_task (see its requirements).
FlowBuilder::emplace must be callable and return a tf::Task; the FlowBuilder instance must be in a valid state to accept new tasks.

tf::Task tf::FlowBuilder::for_each_index(B beg, E end, S inc, C c, P part);
functions.description: Creates and emplaces a Task into the flow that iterates from beg to end with step inc and applies c to each index value, partitioned by part. Internally wraps make_for_each_index_task(beg, end, inc, c, part). Returns the created Task.
requirements: B, E, and S must form a valid index progression accepted by make_for_each_index_task (is_index_range_invalid must be false for work).
C must be invocable as c(idx) where idx is beg + k*inc for k in [0, N).

Internally wraps make_for_each_by_index_task(range, c, part). Returns the created Task.

functions.name: tf::make_reduce_task
functions.signature:
template <typename B, typename E, typename T, typename O, typename P = DefaultPartitioner>
auto tf::make_reduce_task(B b, E e, T& init, O bop, P part = P());
functions.description: Constructs and returns a callable task (lambda) that performs a parallel reduction over the range [b, e). The reduction combines elements by repeatedly applying the binary operation bop to an accumulator init and each dereferenced element. Work is partitioned across Runtime workers using the given partitioner P; partial results are combined into init under a mutex. Intended to be passed to a scheduler (e.g., FlowBuilder::emplace).
requirements: B and E must denote a valid input range [b, e); advancing and distance are used (std::distance, std::advance), so iterators must meet at least the InputIterator requirements.
The accumulator init is passed by reference and will be updated by the task; callers must ensure init remains alive for the task duration.
The binary operation O (bop) must be callable as T bop(T, value_type) and/or T bop(T, T), and return a value assignable to T.
Elements in [b, e) must be dereferenceable; dereferencing must be valid for all positions visited.
Partitioner P must provide the interface used here (type(), chunk_size(), adjusted_chunk_size, loop, operator() wrapper). If not provided, DefaultPartitioner is used.
The task uses concurrency; bop must be safe for use on independent sub-accumulators. Shared updates to init are internally synchronized with a mutex.
If part.type() is STATIC, chunks are sized via adjusted_chunk_size with a minimum of 2 in some paths; in dynamic mode, chunks of size 2 are fetched via an atomic counter.
When N == 1, bop is applied once to init and the single element.

functions.name: tf::make_transform_reduce_task
functions.signature:
template <typename B, typename E, typename T, typename BOP, typename UOP, typename P = DefaultPartitioner>
auto tf::make_transform_reduce_task(B b, E e, T& init, BOP bop, UOP uop, P part = P());
functions.description: Constructs and returns a callable task that performs a parallel transform-reduce over [b, e). Each element is first transformed by uop, then reduced into init using the associative-like binary operation bop. Work is partitioned among Runtime workers via partitioner P; partial results are merged into init under a mutex. Suitable for FlowBuilder::emplace.
requirements: B and E must form a valid input range [b, e); iterators must support std::distance and std::advance (at least InputIterator).
init is passed by reference and must outlive the task; it will be updated by the task.
BOP (bop) must be callable to combine partial results: T bop(T, T) (uses std::move on operands) and return a value assignable to T.
UOP (uop) must be callable as auto uop(*it) and produce a value compatible with bop’s operands (typically T).
Elements in [b, e) must be dereferenceable for the entire traversal.
Partitioner P must implement the interface used (type(), chunk_size(), adjusted_chunk_size, loop, operator() wrapper).
Concurrency is used; transformations and bop on per-thread temporaries must be safe. Final combination into init is internally synchronized.
Handles N == 1 by applying uop to the single element and combining into init with bop.

functions.name: tf::make_transform_reduce_task
functions.signature:
template <typename B1, typename E1, typename B2, typename T, typename BOP_R, typename BOP_T, typename P = DefaultPartitioner, std::enable_if_t<!is_partitioner_v<std::decay_t<BOP_T>>, void>* = nullptr>
auto tf::make_transform_reduce_task(B1 b1, E1 e1, B2 b2, T& init, BOP_R bop_r, BOP_T bop_t, P part = P());
functions.description: Constructs and returns a callable task that performs a parallel transform-reduce over two synchronized ranges. Pairs of elements (*b1_i, *b2_i) are first transformed by bop_t, producing T-like values, then reduced using bop_r into init. Work is partitioned among Runtime workers via P; partial results are merged into init under a mutex. This overload is enabled when BOP_T is not a partitioner type.
requirements: B1 and E1 must denote a valid first range [b1, e1); iterators must support std::distance and std::advance (at least InputIterator).
B2 must be an iterator to the start of a second range with at least std::distance(b1, e1) elements; both ranges are advanced in lockstep.
init is passed by reference and must outlive the task; it will be updated by the task.
BOP_T (bop_t) must be callable as T bop_t(value_type1, value_type2) and return a value compatible with T.
BOP_R (bop_r) must be callable as T bop_r(T, T) (uses std::move on operands) and return a value assignable to T.
Partitioner P must implement the interface used (type(), chunk_size(), adjusted_chunk_size, loop, operator() wrapper).
Dereferencing both ranges must be valid for all visited positions.
Concurrency is used; per-thread temporaries are combined under a mutex into init.
When N == 1, a single pair is transformed and combined into init.

functions.name: tf::make_reduce_by_index_task
functions.signature:
template <typename R, typename T, typename L, typename G, typename P = DefaultPartitioner>
auto tf::make_reduce_by_index_task(R range, T& init, L lop, G gop, P part = P());
functions.description: Constructs and returns a callable task that reduces over an index-based range R using two-stage reduction. Each worker applies lop over subranges of R’s discrete domain to build a temporary optional<T> partial, then all partials are combined into init using gop under a mutex. If the index range is invalid, the task is a no-op.
requirements: R must be a range-like type providing: begin(), end(), step_size(), size(), and discrete_domain(size_t part_b, size_t part_e).
The function is a no-op if is_index_range_invalid(r.begin(), r.end(), r.step_size()) is true.
init is passed by reference and must outlive the task; it will be updated by the task.
L (lop) must be callable as std::optional<T> lop(subrange, std::optional<T>) and return a std::optional<T> representing the partial result for that subrange.
G (gop) must be callable as T gop(T, T) and return a value assignable to T; it combines init with a worker’s partial value.
Partitioner P must implement the interface used (type(), chunk_size(), adjusted_chunk_size, loop, operator() wrapper).
In dynamic partitioning, a worker may receive no work; in that case no combination occurs (tmp is checked before combining).
Concurrency is used; final combination into init is synchronized with a mutex.

functions.name: tf::FlowBuilder::transform_reduce
functions.signature:

Must not be called concurrently with animate/recycle on the same pool instance.

requirements: Type T must be constructible from the provided ArgsT&&...
Type T must provide a member void* _object_pool_block accessible to ObjectPool (e.g., via TF_ENABLE_POOLABLE_ON_THIS).
Returned pointer must be returned to the same pool via recycle; do not free with delete or free.
This function is thread-safe with respect to other animate/recycle calls on the same pool instance.

For std::variant serialization, the currently held alternative will be serialized; the index is written first.

functions.name: tf::make_moc
functions.description: Factory for creating a move-on-copy wrapper (MoC) around a value. The returned MoC<T> stores the provided object and will move its contained object whenever the MoC is copy-constructed, enabling use of move-only or expensive-to-copy objects in copy-oriented APIs. Passing an lvalue will deduce T as an lvalue reference (MoC<X&>), causing the wrapper to hold a reference; passing an rvalue (e.g., std::move(x)) will deduce T as a non-reference (MoC<X>) and move into the wrapper.
requirements: T must be deducible from the argument and constructible from T&& (or T& when deduced from an lvalue).

If the intent is to transfer/move the object into the wrapper, pass an rvalue (e.g., std::move(x)); otherwise, calling with an lvalue will produce a MoC of a reference type and the wrapper will refer to the original object.
The contained type T (or the type referred to) must be movable for MoC's move-on-copy behavior to make sense; on copy, MoC performs std::move(other.object).
The returned MoC<T> type exactly preserves reference qualification from deduction (no decay).

functions.name: tf::visit_tuple
functions.signature:
template <typename Func, typename Tuple, size_t N = 0>
void visit_tuple(Func func, Tuple& tup, size_t idx);
functions.description: Invokes a functor on the element at runtime index idx of a tuple-like object. It linearly recurses at compile time over tuple indices and, when N == idx, calls std::invoke(func, std::get<N>(tup)). If idx is out of range, the function performs no call.
requirements: Tuple must be a tuple-like type compatible with std::tuple_size_v<Tuple> and std::get<N>(Tuple).
Func must be invocable with the selected element type: std::invoke(func, std::get<I>(tup)) must be valid for the chosen index.
idx should be in the range [0, std::tuple_size_v<Tuple>) to trigger a call; otherwise, the function is a no-op.
tup is passed by non-const reference; if func requires const access, ensure Tuple's elements and Func support calling with non-const lvalues or adjust usage accordingly.

functions.name: tf::unroll
functions.signature:
template <auto beg, auto end, auto step, typename F>
void unroll(F f);
functions.description: Template unrolled loop that calls f(i) for a compile-time sequence i = beg, beg+step, ..., stopping before end (i < end). Generates the calls via template recursion, enabling compile-time unrolling in the generated code.
requirements: beg, end, and step are non-type template parameters and must be compile-time constants of the same type, supporting operator< and operator+.
The progression must terminate: there must exist k >= 0 such that beg + k*step >= end; typically, step should be a positive value when beg < end.
F must be invocable with a single argument whose type matches the non-type parameter type (e.g., an integral), i.e., f(beg) must be well-formed.
If the termination condition is not met (e.g., step drives values away from end), compilation may fail due to excessive template instantiation or never terminating recursion.

import random
import string
from typing import List

# Generator for arbitrary string buffers used by many stubs via FUZZ_PARAM_STR.
# We aim to produce strings that are valid and interesting for the Taskflow stubs:
# - Non-empty (many stubs bail on empty)
# - Varied lengths to exercise bounds (1..2048, with bias to small and boundary sizes)
# - Mix of printable, whitespace, punctuation, and some non-printable bytes
# - Occasionally include long repeats or patterned data to influence vector contents
# - Keep total output <= 4096 bytes

PRINTABLE = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + string.punctuation + " \t\n\r"


def _biased_lengths(rng: random.Random) -> List[int]:
    # Include a spread of lengths likely to hit stub limits
    # Common caps seen: 128, 256, 512, 2048
    choices = [1, 2, 3, 7, 15, 31, 63, 64, 65, 100, 127, 128, 129, 200, 255, 256,
               257, 300, 400, 511, 512, 513, 700, 1023, 1024, 1500, 1800, 2047, 2048]
    # Also add a few random lengths
    for _ in range(6):
        choices.append(rng.randint(1, 2048))
    rng.shuffle(choices)
    # Pick 5-8 segments to concatenate later
    k = rng.randint(5, 8)
    return choices[:k]


def _make_segment(rng: random.Random, n: int) -> bytes:
    # Choose a pattern kind
    kind = rng.choice([
        "printable",
        "mixed_bytes",
        "repeated_char",
        "incrementing",
        "zeroes",
        "alternating",
        "hexlike",
    ])
    if n <= 0:
        n = 1

    if kind == "printable":
        return bytes(''.join(rng.choice(PRINTABLE) for _ in range(n)), 'utf-8', 'ignore')

    if kind == "mixed_bytes":
        # Include some non-printable values too
        return bytes(rng.randrange(0, 256) for _ in range(n))

    if kind == "repeated_char":
        c = rng.choice(PRINTABLE)
        return (c.encode('utf-8')) * n

    if kind == "incrementing":
        start = rng.randrange(0, 256)
        return bytes((start + i) % 256 for i in range(n))

    if kind == "zeroes":
        return b"\x00" * n

    if kind == "alternating":
        a = rng.randrange(0, 256)
        b = rng.randrange(0, 256)
        return bytes(a if (i % 2 == 0) else b for i in range(n))

    if kind == "hexlike":
        # Looks like hex but arbitrary length
        hexdigits = string.hexdigits.encode('ascii')
        return bytes(hexdigits[rng.randrange(0, len(hexdigits))] for _ in range(n))

    # Fallback mixed
    return bytes(rng.randrange(0, 256) for _ in range(n))


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    parts: List[bytes] = []

    # Ensure first part is non-empty printable to satisfy stubs that may inspect back() or rely on size>0
    first_len = rng.choice([1, 7, 13, 33, 64, 127, 128, 255, 256])
    parts.append(_make_segment(rng, first_len if first_len > 0 else 1))

    # Add several biased segments
    for L in _biased_lengths(rng):
        seg = _make_segment(rng, L)
        parts.append(seg)

    buf = b"".join(parts)

    # Bound the total size to <= 4096, but keep non-empty
    max_size = 4096
    if len(buf) > max_size:
        # Keep start and end slices to preserve different content and avoid empty
        head_keep = max_size // 2
        tail_keep = max_size - head_keep
        buf = buf[:head_keep] + buf[-tail_keep:]
    if not buf:
        buf = b"A"

    return buf

import os
import random
import string
from typing import List

# We generate interesting environment variable names as bytes.
# The fuzzer stub truncates to 64 chars; we will keep within that bound.
# We focus on POSIX/Windows-friendly names and edge cases.

ALNUM_UNDERSCORE = string.ascii_uppercase + string.ascii_lowercase + string.digits + "_"

COMMON_ENV_VARS: List[str] = [
    # Cross-platform common
    "PATH", "HOME", "USER", "SHELL", "PWD", "TMPDIR", "TEMP", "TMP",
    "LANG", "TERM", "EDITOR", "LOGNAME", "HOSTNAME",
    # Windows common
    "USERNAME", "APPDATA", "LOCALAPPDATA", "ProgramFiles", "SystemRoot",
    # Taskflow/project-related guesses
    "TF_ENABLE_PROFILER", "TF_CPP_VERSION", "TF_NUM_WORKERS",
    # Edge cases
    "_", "_0", "A", "Z", "__",
]


def _random_name(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Choose a pattern to encourage diverse behavior
    choice = rng.random()

    if choice < 0.25:
        # Exact from common list (likely to exist on systems)
        return rng.choice(COMMON_ENV_VARS)
    elif choice < 0.45:
        # Uppercase underscore style typical of env vars
        length = rng.randint(1, 32)
        first = rng.choice(string.ascii_uppercase + "_")
        rest = ''.join(rng.choice(string.ascii_uppercase + string.digits + "_") for _ in range(length-1))
        return first + rest
    elif choice < 0.65:
        # Mixed case with digits and underscores
        length = rng.randint(1, 48)
        return ''.join(rng.choice(ALNUM_UNDERSCORE) for _ in range(length))
    elif choice < 0.80:
        # Prefix/suffix patterns to hit substring lookups
        base = rng.choice(["TF_", "CUDA_", "OMP_", "CXX", "LD_", "DYLD_", "PYTHON", "JAVA", "GIT_"])
        tail_len = rng.randint(0, 24)
        tail = ''.join(rng.choice(ALNUM_UNDERSCORE) for _ in range(tail_len))
        return (base + tail)[:64]
    elif choice < 0.92:
        # Edge cases: minimal and boundary sizes
        variants = [
            "",  # empty string (fuzzer will pass as-is; functions should handle)
            "_", "A", "0",  # single-char
            "A" * 63,  # near limit
            "A" * 64,  # at limit
        ]
        return rng.choice(variants)
    else:
        # Include some unusual but still valid characters for many libc getenv (not strictly portable)
        # Keep to printable non-space symbols often seen in envs
        extra = "-:."  # hyphen, colon, dot sometimes appear
        length = rng.randint(1, 40)
        chars = ALNUM_UNDERSCORE + extra
        return ''.join(rng.choice(chars) for _ in range(length))


def _maybe_set_env(name: str, rng: random.Random) -> None:
    # Occasionally set the variable to present to exercise positive path.
    # Use os.environ to avoid I/O and keep in-process only.
    if not name:
        return
    roll = rng.random()
    if roll < 0.35:
        # Set non-empty value
        val_len = rng.randint(1, 32)
        val_chars = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + "_:-/."
        value = ''.join(rng.choice(val_chars) for _ in range(val_len))
        os.environ[name] = value
    elif roll < 0.45:
        # Set empty value (present but empty) to check API distinction
        os.environ[name] = ""
    elif roll < 0.50:
        # Explicitly ensure absence
        os.environ.pop(name, None)
    # else: leave environment as-is


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    # Generate one environment variable name, optionally influence current process env
    name = _random_name(rng)

    # Optionally manipulate environment to create both present/absent scenarios
    _maybe_set_env(name, rng)

    # Ensure max 64 bytes when encoded; the stub truncates, but we keep it compliant
    # Use ASCII-safe encoding since we only used ASCII chars
    data = name.encode('ascii', errors='ignore')[:64]

    # Guarantee size <= 4096 as required; here it's already small
    return data
